headline: High: Pipecat’s shared-bus, multi-API defaults create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks when paired with a non-runnable docs-only data-engineering artifact.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a docs-only awesome-list with no runtime channel, so it cannot inject directly. Agent B uses a shared bus and multiple input/output services, so if A’s content is copied into B’s prompts or configs, B can be steered by attacker-controlled text. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF operator copies A-sourced text into B prompt templates or message payloads
IF B parses shared-bus content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict B to a separate bus namespace for A-derived content
Add a provenance tag to any A-to-B handoff
Disable stdin/stdout bridging for untrusted text
Review prompt templates for instruction-like file content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B touches text, audio, images, video, and conversation state and can call many third-party APIs. If A is used in the same workspace or copied into B, B may transmit that content off-box through allowlisted network services. The shared workspace is not documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A-derived files or prompts are placed into B’s conversation state
IF B is configured to use any external STT/LLM/TTS provider
mitigations: Keep A artifacts out of B’s workspace
Use only local providers for B during evaluation
Disable logging of conversation state in B
Audit which B providers are enabled
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on B API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is not runnable and has no write surfaces, while B supports shared-bus multi-instance operation but exposes no filesystem or git write capability in the profile. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict is coordination on the shared bus, which is a limited blast-radius issue.
conditions: IF B instances are run concurrently on the same shared bus
IF an external orchestrator maps A outputs into B mutable state
mitigations: Assign each B instance a separate bus topic
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Avoid concurrent runs during testing
Document ownership of shared state keys
requires-engineering: add locking around shared-bus mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated list, not an executor, but B can consume text and act through downstream APIs. If A-derived recommendations are fed into B without verification, B may render or operationalize them as authoritative guidance. Because B has action-capable integrations and the verification step is absent from the profiles, medium is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A-derived text as system or developer instructions
IF B forwards A-derived recommendations into external API actions without human review
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A-derived content
Mark A content as non-authoritative in B prompts
Separate retrieval from action steps
Log every A-to-B transformation
requires-engineering: add verification gates before API execution

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data class or residency mismatch is documented for A, and B’s docs-only profile lists broad modalities but no specific regulated-data handling. The pair therefore shows only a generic compliance gap: B may send content to third-party providers while A is a non-runnable repository. With no explicit PHI/EU PII path, low is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through B’s external providers
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention controls not configured in B
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B inputs
Select providers with matching residency terms
Disable analytics/metrics export
Review retention settings before launch
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data
